blocks.content: When anything about a container looks wrong, docker logs, covered mechanically back in the Docker Containers module, is where debugging almost always starts. This topic focuses on using it effectively.

Before checking resource limits, before inspecting configuration, before anything else, reading a misbehaving container's logs is the fastest way to learn what is actually going wrong, most application errors print something useful to stdout or stderr right before failing.

blocks.alt: The first, fastest diagnostic step, almost every time

blocks.content: A long-running container can accumulate a lot of log output, --tail limits output to the most recent N lines, cutting straight to what just happened instead of scrolling through everything since the container started.

blocks.alt: Jump straight to the recent, relevant output

blocks.content: --since filters by time instead of line count, useful when you know roughly when an issue started, "show me everything from the last 10 minutes" is often more useful than "show me the last 100 lines" for a container with bursty log volume.

blocks.alt: Filtering by when something happened, not just how much

blocks.content: 4. Structured Logs Make This Dramatically Easier
blocks.text: 4. Structured Logs Make This Dramatically Easier

blocks.content: An application that logs structured JSON (one JSON object per line, with fields like level, message, timestamp) is far easier to search and filter reliably than free-form text, piping docker logs output through jq to filter by log level or a specific field turns a wall of text into something actually queryable.

blocks.alt: Structured logs turn a wall of text into something searchable

blocks.content: 5. Where the Logs Actually Come From
blocks.text: 5. Where the Logs Actually Come From

blocks.content: By default, Docker captures logs via the json-file log driver, storing them locally on the host. For production systems, logs are commonly shipped elsewhere instead, to a centralized logging system, via an alternative log driver, so they survive even after a container (and its local logs) is gone.

blocks.alt: Local by default, but easily shipped elsewhere for production

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: docker logs is almost always the fastest first step when debugging a misbehaving container, --tail and --since help narrow in quickly.
Structured JSON logs are dramatically easier to search reliably than free-form text, worth adopting for anything beyond a quick local script.
